page: Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is a Cloud Compute instance configured with 6 shared vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per core. The instance runs on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, utilizing 3 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 320 GB NVMe SSD. The configuration also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a mix of average and weak results, reflecting its shared CPU architecture. Multi-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench ray tracing scoring in the average range. However, single-core capabilities are limited, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and compression tasks placing in the weak to poor categories. Memory read bandwidth is average at 407.68 GB/sec for cached small blocks, but large block write bandwidth drops to a weak 18.72 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and weak single-core performance, this instance is not suited for CPU-intensive or latency-sensitive workloads. However, it offers a cost-effective resource density for multi-threaded applications that can tolerate shared CPU scheduling. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as Redis caching, basic web serving, development environments, and lightweight multi-threaded processing.
description: Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is a Cloud Compute instance configured with 6 shared vCPUs, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a 320 GB NVMe SSD. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz, this instance utilizes 3 physical cores with hyper-threading. Benchmark data shows average multi-core CPU performance and memory read bandwidth, though single-core execution, text processing, and memory write speeds are relatively weak. The instance achieves 6.15 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 5.39 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. The shared CPU allocation makes it a cost-effective option for workloads that do not require dedicated compute resources, making it best suited for general-purpose applications, development environments, and Redis caching.
